newsitem.title: USA: USDA proposes consolidation into 10 milk orders.
newsitem.headline: USDA proposes consolidation into 10 milk orders.

text.p: The Agriculture Department proposed that the current 32 federal milk marketing orders be consolidated into 10 orders, and invited industry and public comment on the proposed consolidation.

The 1996 Farm Bill mandated that the current 32 federal milk orders be consolidated, or merged, into 10 to 14 orders. The Secretary of Agriculure also was directed to designate California as a federal milk order if that state's diary producers petition for and approve such an order.

All reforms must be implemented by April 4,1999. USDA is working with the dairy industry and other parties to develop a proposed rule that will be issued in late 1997. The final rule will be issued in the fall of 1998 and will be voted on by producers.
The USDA proposed the following 10 marketing orders: Pacific Northwest, Western, Southwest, Central, Upper Midwest, Southeast, Mideast, Appalachian, Florida and the Northeast.
